title: A finite purely inseparable extension is a tower of p-th roots
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, $F$ a field of characteristic $p$ and $E/F$ a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] [def-pc-field-extension]. Then there are elements $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n\in E$ ($n\ge0$) with $E=F(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)$ such that for $i=1,\dots,n$, writing $F_{i-1}=F(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{i-1})$ ($F_0=F$): $\alpha_i^p\in F_{i-1}$, $\alpha_i^p$ is not a $p$-th power in $F_{i-1}$, and $[F_{i-1}(\alpha_i):F_{i-1}]=p$. In particular, if $E\ne F$, then $M=F_{n-1}$ is an intermediate field $F\subseteq M\subsetneq E$, finite and purely inseparable over $F$ with $[M:F]<[E:F]$, and $E=M(\beta)$ with $\beta=\alpha_n$, $\beta^p\in M$ not a $p$-th power in $M$, and $E\cong M[z]/(z^p-\beta^p)$ as $M$-algebras, where $M[z]$ is the polynomial ring in one variable over $M$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 09HI (lemma-finite-purely-inseparable, line 1669) and its proof (Lemmas nr-roots-unchanged, take-pth-root); used without citation in the proof of More on Algebra Proposition 07PM ('Let K subset M subset L be a subfield such that L is a degree p extension of M obtained by adjoining a pth root of an element f in M')

proof.text: (The inductive claim and its base.) For an integer $d\ge1$ let $P(d)$ be the assertion: for every field $F$ of characteristic $p$ and every finite purely inseparable extension $E/F$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] with $[E:F]=d$ there are $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n\in E$ as in the first sentence of the statement. We prove $P(d)$ by strong induction on $d$, assuming $P(d')$ for all $1\le d'<d$. If $d=1$, then $F\subseteq E$ is a nonzero $F$-subspace of the $1$-dimensional $F$-space $E$, so $E=F$, and $n=0$ does the job ($E=F_0=F$, no conditions). From now on $d>1$, so $E\ne F$.

If $t=c^p$ with $c\in F$, then, since $p=0$ in $E$ and $p$ divides $ inom pj$ for $0<j<p$, $(\alpha_1-c)^p=\alpha_1^p-c^p=0$, so $\alpha_1-c=0$ in the field $E$ and $\alpha_1=c\in F$, a contradiction. So $t$ is not a $p$-th power in $F$. (The source refers here to Lemma 09H4 'or its proof'; the computation just made is that proof in this case.)

source.place: Fields, proof of Lemma Tag 09HI (lemma-finite-purely-inseparable, line 1669), sentences 3-5

proof.text: ($[F(\alpha_1):F]=p$.) The element $\alpha_1$ is algebraic over $F$ [def-weil-algebraic-element], a root of the nonzero polynomial $x^p-t\in F[x]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis] (fields $F\subseteq E$, $\theta=\alpha_1$), $F(\alpha_1)$ is finite over $F$ and, with $e=[F(\alpha_1):F]\ge1$, the elements $1,\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_1^{e-1}$ form an $F$-basis of $F(\alpha_1)$. Writing $\alpha_1^e=\sum_{j<e}c_j\alpha_1^j$ in this basis gives the monic polynomial $m=x^e-\sum_{j<e}c_jx^j\in F[x]$ of degree $e\ge1$ with $m(\alpha_1)=0$. Every $g\in F[x]$ with $g(\alpha_1)=0$ is divisible by $m$: division by the monic $m$ gives $g=qm+s$ with $\deg s<e$, and $s(\alpha_1)=0$ forces $s=0$ by the linear independence of $1,\dots,\alpha_1^{e-1}$. So $x^p-t=qm$ for some $q\in F[x]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-x-pow-p-minus-t-irreducible] (applicable by Step 2) $x^p-t$ is irreducible; $m$ has degree $e\ge1$, so it is not a nonzero constant, hence $q$ is a nonzero constant. Comparing leading coefficients of the monic polynomials $x^p-t$ and $m$ gives $q=1$, so $m=x^p-t$ and $e=\deg m=p$.

source.place: Fields, proof of Lemma Tag 09HI (lemma-finite-purely-inseparable, line 1669), sentence 6 ('Thus F subset F(alpha) is a subextension of degree p (Lemma 09HF)'), with the minimal-polynomial argument written out

proof.text: ($E/F_1$ is finite purely inseparable of degree $<d$.) Put $F_1=F(\alpha_1)\subseteq E$, a field of characteristic $p$. $E$ is spanned over $F$ by finitely many elements, which then also span $E$ over $F_1\supseteq F$, so $E/F_1$ is finite. Every $x\in E$ has $x^{p^m}\in F\subseteq F_1$ for some $m\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], so $E/F_1$ is purely inseparable. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] for $F\subseteq F_1\subseteq E$ and Step 3, $d=[E:F]=[E:F_1]\,[F_1:F]=p\,[E:F_1]$, so $1\le[E:F_1]=d/p<d$.

source.place: Fields, proof of Lemma Tag 09HI (lemma-finite-purely-inseparable, line 1669), sentence 7 ('By induction ...'): the induction hypothesis applies to E/F(alpha)

proof.text: (Concatenating the towers.) By $P([E:F_1])$ (Step 4) applied to $E/F_1$ there are $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_{k}\in E$ with $E=F_1(\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_k)$ such that, with $G_{j-1}=F_1(\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_{j-1})$, $\gamma_j^p\in G_{j-1}$ is not a $p$-th power in $G_{j-1}$ and $[G_{j-1}(\gamma_j):G_{j-1}]=p$. Put $n=k+1$ and $\alpha_{j+1}=\gamma_j$ for $1\le j\le k$. For $1\le i\le n$, $F(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{i-1})$ and $F_1(\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_{i-2})$ are both the smallest subfield of $E$ containing $F$ and $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{i-1}$ (for $i\ge2$; for $i=1$ the field is $F$), so $F_{i-1}=G_{i-2}$ for $i\ge2$, and $E=F_1(\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_k)=F(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)$. The conditions for $i=1$ are Steps 2 and 3 ($F_0=F$), those for $i\ge2$ are those for $j=i-1$ just obtained. This proves $P(d)$, hence the first assertion for every finite purely inseparable $E/F$.

source.place: Fields, proof of Lemma Tag 09HI (lemma-finite-purely-inseparable, line 1669), last sentence ('The sequence alpha, alpha_1, ..., alpha_n does the job')

proof.text: (In particular: $M$.) Let $E\ne F$ and take $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$ as in the first assertion. If $n=0$ then $E=F_0=F$; so $n\ge1$. Put $M=F_{n-1}$ and $\beta=\alpha_n$: $F\subseteq M\subseteq E$, $E=F_n=M(\beta)$, $\beta^p\in M$ is not a $p$-th power in $M$, and $[E:M]=p$ (clause $i=n$). $M$ is an $F$-subspace of the finite-dimensional $F$-space $E$, hence finite over $F$, and each element of $M$ is an element of $E$, so has a $p$-power power in $F$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]: $M/F$ is finite purely inseparable. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] for $F\subseteq M\subseteq E$, $[E:F]=[E:M][M:F]=p[M:F]>[M:F]$ since $p\ge2$; in particular $M\ne E$.

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 09HI, the last extension of the tower; agent-written consequence

proof.text: (In particular: $E\cong M[z]/(z^p-\beta^p)$.) Let $\varphi:M[z]\to E$ be the $M$-algebra homomorphism $g\mapsto g(\beta)$ of the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis] (fields $M\subseteq E$, $\theta=\beta$, a root of $z^p-\beta^p\in M[z]$) and $[M(\beta):M]=p$ (Step 6), the elements $1,\beta,\dots,\beta^{p-1}$ form an $M$-basis of $M(\beta)=E$; they are $\varphi(1),\dots,\varphi(z^{p-1})$, so $\varphi$ is surjective. Its kernel contains $z^p-\beta^p$. Conversely let $g\in\ker\varphi$; division by the monic $z^p-\beta^p$ gives $g=q\,(z^p-\beta^p)+s$ with $\deg s<p$, and $s(\beta)=g(\beta)=0$ forces $s=0$ by the linear independence of $1,\dots,\beta^{p-1}$. So $\ker\varphi=(z^p-\beta^p)$, and $\varphi$ induces an isomorphism of $M$-algebras $M[z]/(z^p-\beta^p)\cong E$ (first isomorphism theorem).

split_report.summary: Checked against Fields 09HI (fields.tex line 1669) and its proof, with 09HF (line 1617) and 09H4. Seven steps: strong induction on [E:F] with the claim P(d) stated and the base d=1 (step 1); choice of alpha_1 = alpha^{p^{r-1}} with r least, and t = alpha_1^p not a p-th power by the Frobenius computation the source delegates to 09H4 (step 2); [F(alpha_1):F] = p from the power-basis leaf, the division argument for the minimal polynomial written out, and the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-x-pow-p-minus-t-irreducible (09HF, X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_of_prime, KummerPolynomial.lean:99) (step 3); E/F(alpha_1) finite purely inseparable of smaller degree by the definition and the degree-multiplicativity leaf (step 4); concatenation of the towers (step 5); the 'in particular' clause (steps 6-7, agent-written: M = F_{n-1}, M/F finite purely inseparable with [M:F] < [E:F], and E = M[z]/(z^p - beta^p) by evaluation at beta, surjective by the power basis, kernel by division). Statement unchanged except that def-weil-polynomial-ring is now cited for M[z] (added to stmt_deps). Both citers (lem-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-degree-p-intermediate, lem-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-complete-local-regular) use only clauses stated here.
